title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Great Barrier Reef) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict port development and other approvals affecting the Great Barrier Reef world heritage area through changes to national environmental protection law.
It would prohibit specified new ports and developments within existing ports that individually or cumulatively affect the Reef's world heritage values, and require net benefits.
It would also impose an approval moratorium from 20 March 2013 until a strategic assessment was complete and accepted as adequate by the World Heritage Committee.
changes: New ports outside existing port areas along the Reef coastline would be prohibited.
New ports in designated locations identified for protection from industrial development would also be prohibited.
Approval would be barred for developments failing to deliver a net benefit to the world heritage area.
The legislation would commence on Royal Assent.
summary.affected: New port projects, developments within existing ports and other developments affecting the Great Barrier Reef world heritage area are covered.

speeches.speaker: Larissa Waters
speeches.brief: The speaker introduced the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Great Barrier Reef) Bill 2013, which seeks to amend the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 for the Great Barrier Reef. The bill was read a first time.

speeches.speaker: Larissa Waters
speeches.brief: The bill proposes a permanent ban on new port developments outside existing major port areas within or adjoining the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area, a moratorium on new developments until a strategic assessment is completed, and a requirement that projects deliver a net benefit for the reef, to implement World Heritage Committee recommendations and prevent the reef from being added to the World Heritage in Danger list.
